data.answer: NotebookLM MCP authentication uses browser cookies (no official API). The CLI/MCP extracts required cookies (SID/HSID/SSID/APISID/SAPISID and related secure session cookies) from an installed, managed browser session; you authenticate once with `nlm login`, which caches CSRF/session ID and cookies under `~/.notebooklm-mcp-cli/` [1][2]. For Workspace/managed instances, set `NOTEBOOKLM_BASE_URL` (e.g., `https://notebooklm.cloud.google.com`) in your MCP server env config [1]. The underlying NotebookLM base endpoint is a POST to `https://notebooklm.google.com/_/LabsTailwindUi/data/batchexecute` with form fields `f.req` (URL-encoded JSON) and `at` (CSRF token) [3].

data.answer: To authenticate a Salesforce Hosted MCP Server, you must register an External Client App in your org (Connected Apps aren’t supported) and use OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE, per-user context. Create/configure the External Client App, enable OAuth settings, and add the MCP client’s callback URL. Use your saved consumer key (OAuth Client ID) in the MCP client. In Postman, configure OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code with PKCE) with scope mcp_api refresh_token, client ID=consumer key, and callback URL matching the External Client App. [1][2][3][4]

data.answer:
Slack supports four authentication methods for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers: Slack identity auth, Dynamic Client Registration (DCR), manual OAuth, and no authentication [1].

For manual OAuth, you must define an `external_auth_providers` block in your app manifest and reference it via `auth_provider_key` in your `mcp_servers` configuration [1]. The required redirect URI for your OAuth provider is `https://oauth2.slack.com/external/auth/callback` [1][2].

To exchange credentials for an access token, use the Slack user token endpoint: `https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.user.access` [3][4]. Enterprise-managed authorization (EMA) is also available as an alternative to standard OAuth [4].

data.answer: Discord authentication uses either your bot token (from the Bot page) or OAuth2. For API calls with OAuth2, use the Authorization header: “Authorization: Bearer <access_token>” [1][2]. To exchange an OAuth2 authorization code for a token, POST to https://discord.com/api/oauth2/token with grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, and (per docs) include client_id/client_secret via HTTP Basic or form data [3][4]. For client-credentials (bot testing), POST to https://discord.com/api/oauth2/token with grant_type=client_credentials using HTTP Basic with client_id/client_secret [3]. For RPC, call AUTHORIZE to get a code, then exchange via /oauth2/token [4].

data.answer: Neo4j MCP authentication (HTTP transport) uses per-request credentials via the HTTP headers. Configure your MCP client to send either Authorization: Bearer <token> (for Neo4j Enterprise/Aura with OAuth/SSO; token is not base64) or Authorization: Basic <base64(username:password)>. In mcp.json, set the HTTP server to type "http" and provide the Authorization header; by default the MCP server reads Authorization, but you can override it with NEO4J_HTTP_AUTH_HEADER_NAME or --neo4j-http-auth-header-name. Community Edition doesn’t support bearer, use Basic Auth. [1][2]

data.answer:
Notion MCP requires user-based OAuth 2.0 authentication and does not support bearer token authentication. To connect an MCP client to Notion, you must implement the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE.

The process involves discovering the server's OAuth metadata, generating PKCE parameters, performing dynamic client registration, and exchanging the authorization code for tokens. Once authenticated, you include the access token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token when connecting to the Notion MCP server via Streamable HTTP or SSE.
